content.value_statement: Teams need consistent commit messages that link changes to issues. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to draft Sentry-style commits.
actual_capabilities: Formats commit messages with type, optional scope, subject, body, and footer sections.
Applies Sentry-friendly Conventional Commit types such as feat, fix, ref, docs, test, and chore.
Adds issue reference footers for GitHub, Sentry, and Linear style identifiers.
Suggests Claude co-author attribution when changes were primarily AI-generated.
Provides formats for simple fixes, features, refactors, breaking changes, and reverts.
Reminds users to work from a feature branch before committing changes.
limitations: It does not inspect the git diff unless the user or assistant provides the change details.
Sentry conventions may not match every repository or organization policy.
Branch command examples can change local git state if a user chooses to run them.
It does not verify issue identifiers against GitHub, Sentry, Linear, or other services.

use_cases.title: Prepare Reviewable Commits
use_cases.description: Turn a focused code change into a clear commit message with a subject, body, and issue footer.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team History
use_cases.description: Keep commit messages consistent across a repository that follows Sentry-style Conventional Commit rules.

use_cases.title: Document AI-Assisted Changes
use_cases.description: Add the recommended co-author footer when a coding assistant produced most of the change.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Commit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for one focused change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Sentry-style commit message for this change: [describe the change]. Use the correct type and keep the subject concise.

prompt_templates.title: Add an Issue Reference
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for linking work to tracking systems.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a Sentry-style commit message for [change summary]. Include the issue reference [issue ID] and choose Fixes or Refs correctly.

prompt_templates.title: Shape a Commit From a Diff
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt when the assistant can inspect repository changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current changes and write one Sentry-style commit message. Explain what changed and why, not implementation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Complex History
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for breaking changes, reverts, or AI-authored work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the final commit message for this change. Include breaking-change or revert wording if needed, plus Claude co-author attribution if appropriate.

output_examples.input: A bug fix adds a null check for deleted user accounts and closes SENTRY-5678.
output_examples.output: A fix commit with an API scope, a short subject, a body explaining the crash prevention, a SENTRY footer, and Claude attribution when needed.

output_examples.input: A feature sends alert updates as replies in an existing Slack thread and references GH-1234.
output_examples.output: A feature commit with an alerts scope, a body explaining grouped notifications, and a reference footer that links the GitHub issue.

output_examples.input: A breaking change removes deprecated v1 endpoints and closes SENTRY-9999.
output_examples.output: A breaking-change commit with a clear subject, migration context in the body, a breaking-change footer, and the closing issue reference.

best_practices: Keep each commit focused on one stable, reviewable change.
Use imperative present tense and keep the subject under the stated length limit.
Use the footer to link issues and record AI co-author attribution when appropriate.
anti_patterns: Do not mix unrelated fixes, features, and refactors in one commit message.
Do not add generic AI disclosure text outside the approved co-author footer.
Do not use Fixes when the commit should only reference an issue without closing it.

faq.question: Does this skill create commits automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides commit message guidance. The user or assistant still decides whether to run git commands.

faq.question: Which commit format does it use?
faq.answer: It uses a Sentry-style Conventional Commit format with type, optional scope, subject, body, and footer.

faq.question: Can it reference GitHub and Sentry issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for GitHub numbers, Sentry issue keys, and Linear references.

faq.question: How should AI-generated changes be marked?
faq.answer: Use the Claude co-author footer when changes were primarily generated by a coding assistant.

faq.question: Does it validate issue IDs?
faq.answer: No. It shows the expected footer patterns but does not contact external issue trackers.

faq.question: Is it specific to Sentry repositories?
faq.answer: It is optimized for Sentry conventions, but many rules also help teams using Conventional Commits.
